 JUDGMENT
The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- for the death of Mr.Mahesh Kumar in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioners' case are as under:
2. That on 27.09.2021 at about 5-12 to 5-20 a.m. deceased Mahesh Kumar was riding the motor bike bearing No.TN-70-Y-5779 when he was proceeding at Thali, Hosur Main Road, Bengaluru, at that time, driver of Tipper lorry bearing registration No.KA-51-AF-1690 drove the same with high speed in a rash and negligent mannerand dashed against the motor vehicle bearing NO. KA-57- AF-1690.
Due to the impact, Mahesh Kumar sustained grievous injuries and died at the spot.
Thereafter, post mortem was conducted and the dead body was handed over to the petitioners.

Subsequently, the petitioners had spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral,
obsequies ceremonies and other incidental expenses.

3. It is further stated that, prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 38 years and was working as driver and earning Rs.25,000/- per month and in addition to that he was earning Rs.5,000/- per month as over time work and contributing entire income towards the welfare of the family.

Due to untimely death of the deceased, life of the petitioners became dark,
miserable and put to great financial hardship.
4. It is further contended that, the accident occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of the lorry bearing registration No.KA-51-AF-1690.
In this regard, Mathigiri Police registered the case against the driver of the said vehicle in Crime No.339/2021.
As such, the respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.

sentences.text: In response to the notice, The respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and respondent No.1 filed the written statement.
But respondent No.2 has not filed written statement.
respondent No.3 has not appeared before this tribunal, remained absent, hence placed exparte.
6. In the written statement, the respondent No.1 has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further, this respondent has admitted about issuance of insurance policy in respect of lorry bearing registration No.KA-51-AF-1690 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

It is also contention of the respondent No.1 that, the alleged accident took place on 27.09.2021, however the complaint was lodged on 28.09.2021 after the lapse of 1 days from the date of alleged accident.

It is also contention of the respondent No.1 that, the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective D.L. as on the date of the accident and was not having valid permit to ply in the pace of the accident.
It is the defence of the respondent No.2 that, the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of the deceased himself and not on the part of the driver of offending vehicle.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and relationship between deceased with the petitioners.
Ultimately contended that the claim of the petitioners is highly excessive, exorbitant and arbitrary.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.

7. On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, this tribunal has framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that, Mahesh Kumar died due to the injuries sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 27.09.2021 at about 5.15 to 5.20 a.m. at Thali, Hosur Main Road, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Lorry bearing registration No.KA-51- AF-1690 in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?
3) What order or award?

8. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioners, the petitioner No.1 examined herself as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P25.
9.

On the other hand, respondent No.2 has examined its AVP as RW1 and got marked the document at Ex.R1 to Ex.R3 and also examined Akshaya C.M., FDA, RTO, Electronic city as RW.2 and got marked the document at Ex.R4 and Ex.R5.
10.
Heard the arguments and perused the materials available on record.

Consequently, Mahesh Kumar died in the said accident.
As such, they have filed this claim petition against the respondents.

On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the deceased and not on the part of the driver of the lorry bearing registration No.KA-51-AF-1690.
15.

On the basis of rival contention of both the parties, first of all, the petitioners have to place satisfactory evidence on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities against the driver of the offending vehicle in question.
16. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 by name Ramya A. got examined as PW1.
In her examination-in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioners in support of oral evidence of PW.1 have relied upon the police documents at Ex.
P1 to Ex.11
On going through the documents, Ex.P1- true copy of the F.I.R. in Crime No.339/2021 of Mathigiri Police Station.

Ex.P2-true copy of the first information statement given by the respondent No.3 by name Thyagarajan i.e., father of deceased, Ex.P3- spot mahazar, Ex.P4-true copy of sketch,
Ex.P 5 and 6-true copy IMV reports, Ex.P7- Arrest Card, Ex.P8-true copy of Witness list,
Ex.P9-statement of witnesses, Ex.P10-PM report and Ex.P11-true copy of charge sheet.

18. On perusal of the police documents it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by the respondent No.3, the S.H.O. of Mathigiri Traffic P.S. registered the case against the driver of lorry bearing registration No.KA-51-AF- 1690 for the offences punishable under Sections 279 & 304(A) of IPC.

After investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against driver of the lorry vehicle alleging that driver has committed the offences punishable under section 279 & 304(A)
of IPC.
19.
On the other hand, the respondents have taken contention that the accident was not occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry.
In this regard respondent No.1 has examined its AVP of the Insurance company as RW1.
RW.1 has reiterated the averments made in the written statement.
In his cross examination he has stated that he is giving evidence on the basis of documents.
Therefore his oral evidence is not helpful to respondent No.1.
Further the respondent No.1 has not examined either the driver of the offending vehicle or any of the independent eye witness, who witnessed the alleged accident.
Hence, the contention taken by the respondent No.1 cannot be accepted.

20. Apart from this, PW1 was subjected for cross-examination, but no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondent No.1 about the denial of allegation made against the driver of the offending vehicle.
21. In the light of the evidence placed by petitioners, I am of the view that, the petitioners have placed satisfactory and acceptable evidence to prove the above issue.

Hence, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry bearing No.KA-51-AF-1690 and in the said accident, Mahesh Kumar succumbed to the injuries.

ISSUE No.2:
22.

Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.

Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.

At the same time, the documents produced by the petitioners, to prove their relationship with the deceased marked at Ex.P16 to Ex.P18 i.e., birth certificate of the petitioner No.2 and Aadhar cards of the deceased and the petitioner No.1 and 2 have not been disputed by the other side.
The recitals of the above documents clearly speak about the relationship between the petitioners, respondent No.3 and the deceased.

23. Another aspect to be considered herein that, on going through the particulars of the petitioners mentioned in the cause title of the petition reflected that, the petitioner No.1 being the wife has lost her husband and the petitioner No.2 being the daughter of the deceased have lost their love and affection of their father and respondent No.3 being father of deceased has lost his son, who was the backbone of the family.
Hence, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners and respondent No.3 were dependents on the deceased during his lifetime.
24. The petitioners herein, have placed driving licence, which is marked at Ex.P13 to prove the actual age of the deceased as on the date of the accident.
On going through the said documents, the date of birth of the deceased has been mentioned as 06.11.1986.
But the petitioners have shown the age of the deceased as 38 years.
The accident occurred on 27.09.2021.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the deceased was aged about 38 years.

For his age, multiplier '15' is applicable as per the ratio in "Sarala Verma" Case.
25.
In connection with the work of the deceased, in the main petition and also in the evidence of PW1 stated that, deceased was working as a driver and was earning of Rs.30,000/- per month.
The petitioners have not placed any documents to show the income of the deceased.
Hence, in the absence of the definite income of the deceased, it is opt to consider the notional income as per law.
It is pertinent to note that, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2021.
By keeping in mind about the year of the accident and also notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.15,000/- for the year 2021.
26. Apart from this, it is also relevant to discuss, that the Honourable Supreme Court in the decision reported in, 2018 SAR (Civil) 81.

National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others,
"

sentences.text: It was observed that, "While determining the income, an addition of 50 per cent of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30 per cent, if the age of the deceased was between 40 and 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 and 60 years, the addition should be 15 per cent.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.

6 case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40 per cent of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.

sentences.text: An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years.

An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 and 50 years and 10 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 50-60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component. "

27. Having considered the above, as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/3 rd) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/4 th where the number of dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5 th ) where the number of the dependent family members exceeds six."
28. In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, there are five persons were depending upon the income of the deceased.
Hence, as per the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case at para No.14, 1/4th has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation.
29. In the present case, deceased was aged about 38 years as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "15" is applicable.

And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through the nature of the occupation forthcoming in the petition averments, it is evident that, the deceased herein is not having permanent job and accurate income for consideration.
As such, deceased was comes under the purview of below 40 years, 40% income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects.
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.15,000/- per month.
Annual income of the deceased was Rs.1,80,000/- per year.
Along with this, the future prospects of 40% is to be taken in to consideration, then the annual income of the deceased comes to (Rs.1,80,000+72,000) = Rs.2,52,000/-.
And 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.

Thus, net loss of income comes to Rs.1,68,000/-
(Rs.2,52,000-Rs.84,000).

This income has to be multiplied by multiplier "15" which comes to Rs.25,20,000/-.
30.

Apart from this aspect, in connection with the loss of estate, consortium and with respect to the funeral expenses to calculate the quantum of the compensation under the aforesaid heads, it is relevant to note herein the following authority;
2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited.
V/ s Pranay Sethi and others,
The Hon'ble Apex Court discussed various aspects in connection with the claim petition filed by the claimants for compensation.

And also observed that while determining the claim petition, the reasonable figures on conventional heads, viz., loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

LIABILITY:
34.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry bearing registration No.KA-51-AF-1690, alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioners in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.

The respondent No.1 has taken specific defence that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid DL to drive the medium goods carrier transport vehicle and thereby respondent No.2 has violated terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

To prove this contention the respondent No.1 has examined FDA, RTO, Electronic city Bengaluru as RW.2 and got marked Ex.R4 and Ex.R5, Ex.R4 is authorization letter and Ex.R5 is DL extract of driver of vehicle of respondent No.2.
On perusal of Ex.R5 it appears that the offending vehicle driver was having LMV licence, as on the date of accident.
Further, the driver has obtained transport vehicle licence after the date of accident on 20.11.2023 which is valid till 19.11.2028.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for petitioner has argued that as per Ex.P12, vehicle bearing No.KA-51-AF- 1690 s medium goods vehicle having unladen weight 3750.
It is below the 7500 cc.
Therefore, the driver of the offending vehicle was not barred to drive the offending vehicle.
In case, Tribunal come to conclusion that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid DL at the time of accident,
then prays to consider pay and recovery principle and has also relied above cited decisions.

36. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.1 has relied supra decisions and prays to consider that as on the date of accident driver of the offending vehicle was not valid licence to drive the vehicle as on the date of accident.

37. Ongoing through the citations relied by the learned counsel for respondent No.1, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that to drive goods carriage vehicle, the driver of the vehicle is required to possess specific licence to drive the clause of vehicle described in Sec.10 of MV Act.
In this case also the driver of the offending vehicle was only having LMV licence and not transport licence as per Ex.R5 as on the date of accident.
Therefore it is violation of terms and condition of insurance policy.

Therefore, respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation of Rs.26,85,000/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
38. But, as per Ex.R2 insurance policy was valid from 01.10.2020 to 30.09.2021.
The alleged accident had taken place on 27.09.2021.
As on the date of accident insurance policy was in existence.

By relying the principle laid down in the case of National Insurance company Ltd., V/s.
Swaran Sing and others

ISSUE No.3:
39.
In view of my due discussions on Issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.26,85,000/- (Rupees twenty six lakhs eighty five thousand only), from the date of petition till its realisation.

The respondent No.1-Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order, thereafter recover the same from the respondent No.2 through due process of law.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 is entitled for the share of 70%, the petitioner No.2 is entitled the share of 20% and the respondent No.3 is Ramya .A vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51536813/

The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- for the death of Mr.Mahesh Kumar in a road traffic accident.

opennyai_summary.issue:
7. On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, this tribunal has framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that, Mahesh Kumar died due to the injuries sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 27.09.2021 at about 5.15 to 5.20 a.m. at Thali, Hosur Main Road, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Lorry bearing registration No.KA-51- AF-1690 in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?
3) What order or award?
opennyai_summary.arguments:
At the time of argument the learned counsel for the petitioners have relied the following decisions;
1. (2004) 3 SCC 297 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Swaran Singh And others.
2. (2018) 3 SCC 208 in between Pappu and others V/s. Vinod Kumar Lamba and another.
3. MFA No. 9827/2012 Decided on 12.01.2024 in between The New India Assurance Co. Ltd., V/.
Smt. Radhika and Others.
I have gone through the supra decisions the principle laid down in the supra decisions is that in case driver of offending vehicle has no valid DL to drive the vehicle at the time of accident then the insurance company has to pay award amount to the victims and same recover from owner of the vehicle.
12.
In this case also the driver of the offending vehicle was only having LMV licence and not transport licence as per Ex.R5 as on the date of accident.
Therefore it is violation of terms and condition of insurance policy.
Therefore, respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation of Rs.26,85,000/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.
Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.
At the same time, the documents produced by the petitioners, to prove their relationship with the deceased marked at Ex.P16 to Ex.P18 i.e., birth certificate of the petitioner No.2 and Aadhar cards of the deceased and the petitioner No.1 and 2 have not been disputed by the other side.
The recitals of the above documents clearly speak about the relationship between the petitioners, respondent No.3 and the deceased.
The petitioners have not placed any documents to show the income of the deceased.
Hence, in the absence of the definite income of the deceased, it is opt to consider the notional income as per law.
27. Having considered the above, as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/3 rd) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/4 th where the number of dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5 th ) where the number of the dependent family members exceeds six."

38. But, as per Ex.R2 insurance policy was valid from 01.10.2020 to 30.09.2021.
The alleged accident had taken place on 27.09.2021.

By relying the principle laid down in the case of National Insurance company Ltd., V/s.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.15,000/- per month.
Along with this, the future prospects of 40% is to be taken in to consideration, then the annual income of the deceased comes to (Rs.1,80,000+72,000) = Rs.2,52,000/-.
And 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
Accordingly, the petitioners herein are entitled to get total compensation of Rs.26,85,000/-
(Rupees twenty six lakhs eighty five thousand only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka in MFA No.
103557/2016, Between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 is Partly Affirmative.

The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
